summary: compat-es fix round: all 20 review findings handled. 18 fixed with regression tests. 1 was already fixed by a concurrent edit (painless doc['ul'].value). 1 was only partly reproducible (_termStats query_string counts): the linear-time fix and the query_string lenient fix are done, and the rest comes from a separate query_string whitespace-grouping gap (listed in remaining). Critical items: (1) searches now run off the tokio reactor, so GET / and _cluster/health stay responsive during a long search, and they are cancelled when the client disconnects; (2) a Painless catch can no longer swallow a timeout or cancellation; (3) every H3 address from a peer is validated, so the geo_grid query and processor no longer panic. Runtime fields: composite sub-fields work, mapping runtime fields shadow concrete fields, request runtime fields sort at the coordinator, sorts honour mode, missing and ip, every query type is supported with each type's value parsing and ES's error texts, and definitions are validated (request runtime_mappings per shard, mapping scripts compiled at mapping time). Also done: ES timeout semantics (scroll, ms granularity, search.default_search_timeout), no fabricated hits from a timed-out script sort, loop statement limits per script context as ES 9.5 sets them (and everywhere in the OpenSearch dialect), simulate on self-referencing documents, fields format beating docvalue_fields, geo_grid validation texts, linear _termStats, cached runtime fields per mapping (200 runtime fields: term query 19.9 -> 5.5 ms in a debug build). New fixture compat_es_r5.json has 181 steps captured from ES 9.5.5, all green. YAML ES 3809/3905 and OpenSearch 1455/1506, 0 regressions in both.
public_api: search-es: `pub async fn rest::handle_shared(cluster: &Arc<Cluster>, req: EsRequest) -> EsResponse`. Search APIs run on a blocking thread with an ambient SearchControl whose `cancelled` flag is set when the future is dropped; anything else goes to handle. `handle` itself runs search APIs inside tokio::task::block_in_place on multi-thread runtimes. search::runtime: `RuntimeScope::build(&Arc<ScriptService>, Arc<ClusterState>, &IndexMeta, &Arc<FieldTable>, shard, Option<&Map>) -> EsResult<Option<Arc<RuntimeScope>>>`: request fields are compiled eagerly, mapping fields lazily. Also `RuntimeScope::{ambient, is_for, index_name, get -> Option<Arc<Evaluator>>, field, fields, shadows}`, `RuntimeFields::of_index(&Arc<Mapping>, req)` (cached per mapping), `Evaluator::counted()`, `SortMissing`, `sort_key(ev, searcher, reverse, SortMode, SortMissing)`, `check_mapping_scripts(scripts, st, mapping)` and `Predicate::{TermsIgnoreCase, PrefixIgnoreCase, Automaton, Ips, Bool}`. New module search::runtime_query provides QueryCtx::{runtime_dispatch, runtime_target, runtime_prefix, runtime_wildcard, runtime_match}. search::scripts: `search_scripts_poll()`, `CancelHost::{ambient, prepare}`, and `Painless.counted: bool` (struct literals need it). search::sort::merge_keys(keys, formats). search::extra::geotile_zxy (pub(crate)). ScriptTerms::runtime(ev, searcher, reverse, SortMode, SortMissing), plus the pub fields ip and missing_first(). search-aggs: `h3::is_valid(u64) -> bool`. `h3::string_to_h3` now returns only valid cells. New `h3::string_to_h3_lenient`. search-index: unchanged API; the TopFieldCollector stops with the interruption error instead of collecting a doc whose sort script was interrupted. search-painless: unchanged API; check_cancelled failures are uncatchable. search-server: node.rs calls search_es::rest::handle_shared.
done: F1 critical, slow search blocks the node. rest/mod.rs dispatch_off_reactor runs search APIs (search, msearch, count, explain, scroll, templates, termvectors, validate, terms_enum, rank_eval, mvt, fleet, rollup, search_application, graph, eql, esql, sql, open PIT) in block_in_place, so the worker's other connections move to another thread. The new handle_shared runs them via spawn_blocking with a CancelOnDrop guard, so a client disconnect sets SearchControl.cancelled. query_phase merges that flag into its control. Verified: _cluster/health answers in 18 ms during a 15 s search, and an infinite-loop search stops burning CPU after the client times out.

F2 critical, catch(Exception) swallows the deadline. vm.rs cancelled_error makes check_cancelled failures uncatchable, both in loops and in library-driven lambdas. Test guards.rs scripts_cannot_catch_cancellation. Verified: the reviewer's while(true){try{...}catch} script with timeout=500ms answers timed_out:true in 0.52 s.

F3 critical, H3 panics. search-aggs h3 is_valid_cell (H3.h3IsValid); string_to_h3 is strict and string_to_h3_lenient accepts readable indices (the processor's ES behaviour for '0'). geo_grid processor: unreadable index gives 'invalid tile definition' caused by reason null; finest cells fail only when children_field ('Invalid child resolution [15]') or non_children_field ('Resolution overflow') is asked for. The query rejects invalid cells and '0' with 'Invalid h3 address'. Test search-aggs tests/h3.rs invalid_addresses_are_rejected plus a processors.rs unit test.
F4 composite runtime fields: EvalLeaf looks up emitted values by the full sub-field name. fields, term, terms agg, sum and sort on composite sub-fields match ES.

F5 mapping runtime fields shadow concrete fields in queries (QueryCtx::runtime_field), scripts' doc[...] (RuntimeScope shadowing set), aggregations (the mod.rs agg def check) and fetch (an empty runtime result removes the concrete value).
F6 sorts on request runtime_mappings resolve at the coordinator: the 3 sort::build sites in the reduce set qctx.runtime_mappings.

F7 runtime sorts: NumberSort honours mode (min/max/sum/avg/median, longs rounded as MultiValueMode) and missing (_first/_last/number). ScriptTerms runtime does min/max by mode, missing _first or a custom value, and ip values as 16-byte addresses rendered as ips. sort::merge_keys merges string-ordinal sorts as keyword keys with missing last/first, which fixes the cross-shard null misorder. geo_point runtime sort gives ES's error.

F8/F9 runtime queries (new search/runtime_query.rs): term (case_insensitive), terms, range, exists, prefix (case_insensitive), wildcard, regexp (case_insensitive gives 'Match flags not yet implemented [256]'), fuzzy, match/match_phrase/match_bool_prefix (phrase prefix errors), query_string/simple_query_string (hooks in prefix_query, wildcard_query and text::field_query) and terms_set. Values are parsed with each type's rules: long decimals and range rounding, out-of-range texts, dates with format, date math and now (parse_exception on bad input), ip CIDR and the 'Illegal prefix length' text (also fixed for concrete ip fields in engine/ranges.rs cidr), boolean parseBoolean and ES's range table. ES errors are reproduced for unsupported queries per type and for geo_point term/range.

F10 validation: RuntimeScope::build compiles request fields eagerly, so the shard fails on a bad type, unknown parameter, compile error or bad on_script_error even with size:0. RuntimeField::parse checks on_script_error values and 'requires field [script]'. New: mapping runtime scripts are compiled when an index is created or a mapping is put ('Failed to parse mapping: compile error'), as ES does.
F11 timeouts: search_deadline gives no deadline for scrolls or -1, whole-millisecond granularity (timeout=0 lets a fast search finish) and falls back to search.default_search_timeout.

F12 a timed-out _script sort no longer returns a fabricated hit: the search-index TopFieldLeaf stops with the interruption when a sort script was interrupted. Test collectors.rs interrupted_sort_scripts_keep_partial_results_only.

F13 loop statement limits per context, as ES 9.5.5 sets _setCancellationCheck. No limit: script_score query, script query, _script sorts, agg value scripts, scripted_metric init/map/combine/reduce and bucket_script/bucket_selector (CancelHost), script_fields, runtime field queries, terms_set and interval filters. Limit: function_score script functions (Painless.counted) and runtime fields evaluated as field data in fetch, aggs, sorts and doc[] reads (Evaluator::counted). The OpenSearch dialect counts everywhere (search_scripts_poll). All 13 contexts match ES.
F14 _simulate with a self-referencing doc returns ES's error (non-verbose), and in verbose mode every processor from that point reports the error.
F15 runtime fields: the fields format wins over docvalue_fields.

F16 geo_grid query: geohash 'empty geohash' at parse, only the first 12 chars read; geotile parse errors with the NumberFormatException cause; precision error before the range check; x/y range checked on the raw ints. The processor uses the same geotile validation.

F17 _termStats collection uses a HashSet (linear). query_string lenient is the default when fields contains '*' and honours index.query_string.lenient. The reviewer's exact count diff was not reproducible with the mappings tried; the remaining diffs are caused by query_string whitespace grouping (see remaining).

F18 runtime fetch reuses the shard's RuntimeScope (no RuntimeFields::of or compile per hit). RuntimeScope compiles mapping fields lazily. Parsed mapping runtime sections are cached per Arc<Mapping>, with a shared default DateFormatter. With 200 mapping runtime fields (debug build): term query 19.9 -> 5.5 ms (2.5 ms without runtime fields), fields:[r1] 278 -> 17 ms.
F19 search-painless execute::documents: already green (fixed by a concurrent unsigned_long_allowlist edit); all search-painless tests pass.

F20 clippy: search-aggs format.rs stray #[test] fixed, so the decimals test runs again. Fixed engine/fields.rs sort_by_key, document/fast/tests.rs is_multiple_of, #[allow(clippy::items_after_test_module)] in api/snapshots.rs and query/xparser.rs, and search-codec merge.rs needless_range_loop. The remaining reviewer items (query_string type_complexity, esql collapsible_if, the sql lib test) are no longer reported.
Fixture crates/search-es/tests/fixtures/docs/compat_es_r5.json: 181 steps captured from ES 9.5.5 (runtime fields, loop limits, geo_grid, termStats, simulate, mapping validation), all green.
Docs: compatibility.md module-suite numbers (581/760, runtime_fields 169/245); contracts.md handle_shared and h3 validity.
remaining: query_string doesn't group consecutive bare terms as Lucene's parser with splitOnWhitespace=false does. ES analyzes 'foo bar' as one chunk per field: a keyword field gets the term 'foo bar' and a text field gets (a:foo a:bar). Roll builds (a:foo | a.keyword:foo) (a:bar | a.keyword:bar), so a keyword match is missed and explanations and _termStats counts differ. Fix in search/query_string.rs Parser::query by merging bare-term runs into one field_text call.

Searches aren't registered as tasks: _tasks doesn't list indices:data/read/search, and _tasks/_cancel can't cancel one. The ambient SearchControl.cancelled flag from handle_shared is the hook to wire to TaskRegistry. Graceful shutdown still waits for a running search that has no timeout.
No bounded search thread pool: block_in_place/spawn_blocking are limited only by tokio's 512 blocking threads. ES queues and rejects with 429 es_rejected_execution_exception.

Ingest maps created by processors keep insertion order in ES (LinkedHashMap) but roll orders every nested map by Java HashMap order. Example: geo_grid GeoJSON prints coordinates before type; the fixture marks these steps unordered.
The geo_grid processor doesn't split dateline-crossing H3 cells into a MultiPolygon (geohex '0' differs; pre-existing).
_termStats for a terms query on a text field with duplicate values: ES reports 0 unique terms, roll 2 (unexplained).
Timed-out searches: roll's total counts docs up to the interruption, while ES's count shortcut (Weight.count) reports all of them.
Smaller runtime cost: each shard still builds the RuntimeScope evaluator map and shadowing set (O(runtime fields) string clones per shard). These could move into the cached per-mapping struct.

notes_for_others: server: search-server node.rs now calls search_es::rest::handle_shared(&loaded.cluster, req), so search APIs run on blocking threads and are cancelled on client disconnect. Lease/fair permits drop with the request future, while a cancelled search may still be finishing for a moment on its blocking thread.

Everyone: do not leave your own search-dev listening inside the ROLL_PORT range you pass to search-yaml-suites.sh. The runner treats an already-listening port as its own server (my dev server on 19501 made the OpenSearch suite show false regressions).
